spec.title: PROP-019: Organization consumer licensing and distribution evidence

status.comment: trusted policy data foundation; consumer scanning and artifact enforcement remain open

p.ORGANIZATION-POLICY-FORMAT: codkitOrganizationPolicy:1 declares organization profile ID/revision, own holders and license expression, approved/forbidden third-party expressions, approved exceptions, a LicenseRef namespace, exact canonical custom-license texts with SHA-256, distribution notice/SBOM/carrier requirements and optional legal-review reference and optional trusted standardLicenseTexts for standard license/approved-exception notice text. Standard text records require installed SPDX IDs or approved exception IDs, unique identities, nonempty LF-only text with final LF and exact SHA-256; profiles omitting this field retain their previous parsed bytes. The schema is strict and types derive from it. SPDX identifiers come from the installed list. NOASSERTION, undeclared/foreign-namespace LicenseRef and missing/changed text/hash refuse. Custom texts are LF-only with a final LF and no BOM. This profile applies to consumer scope and never weakens Codkit's separate installed supply policy.

p.ORGANIZATION-POLICY-TRUST: A user/admin composition root supplies the policy directory; the default is the user .codkit directory. organization-policies.json carries codkitOrganizationPolicyStore:1 and policy records. Store reads use contained regular-file I/O, validate every profile and refuse conflicting IDs including case aliases. A directory inside the physical patchset or an alias resolving into it refuses. No cwd/patchset fallback or patchset-supplied policy path is accepted. The selected policy and raw store bytes each receive their own digest; a digest is not an invented signature or legal approval.

p.ORGANIZATION-POLICY-SELECTION: Patchset selection contains only profile ID and optional additionalForbidden expressions. Holders, allowlists, license text, policy locations and other authority fields refuse. Additional prohibitions are monotone and cannot enable a license. Own scope uses the exact declared own expression; third-party scope uses exact approved expression combinations and forbidden identifiers/expressions. AND/OR/WITH and bounded parentheses are syntax, never automatic inference of legal permissions; an OR combination not explicitly approved remains refused.

p.CONSUMER-LICENSE-CHECK: Consumer source scanning uses the same sidecar/override/header/annotation precedence and nested REUSE matching as supply scanning, but its readers prove contained regular-file paths and its permission verdicts come only from the selected organization policy. All stated copyright holders must be organization holders for own scope; mixed/foreign holders remain third-party, with provenance annotation required. Modifications copyright does not replace upstream ownership. Exactly one SPDX expression and own copyright year are required; orphan sidecars and source symlinks refuse. Carrier/annotation license and foreign-holder disagreement refuse; third-party provenance requires a nonempty origin comment and binds the actual REUSE registry path/bytes/copyright/comment. Own sidecars/override annotations cannot erase declared upstream ownership in the original header. Checked source bytes, exact carrier path/bytes and selected policy digest bind a deterministic codkitConsumerLicenseCheck:1 report. Existing Codkit supply rules and default carrier readers remain unchanged; consumer-specific permissions never alter the supply authority.

p.CONSUMER-LICENSE-CLI: `codkit license consumer-check <dir> --profile <id>` inspects the explicit source directory read-only. A resolved patchset root is required solely to enforce the trusted-store boundary; neither fork nor codkit.json nor adapter execution is needed. The operator selects only a profile ID; the policy store is the fixed user ~/.codkit/organization-policies.json, without cwd/patchset fallback or a policy-directory flag. JSON data is the versioned consumer report, codes are 0 complete, 1 incomplete source evidence and 2 invalid invocation or unavailable trusted profile. The existing supply `license check` remains separate and unchanged.

p.DISTRIBUTION-NOTICE-CHECK: Notice attachment inspection captures the actual declared distribution inventory before and after reads. Each directory output carries every policy-required notice at its root; file outputs carry notices as separately declared sibling output files. A notice existing only in source, in another bundle or below the bundle root does not satisfy attachment. Notice-only or empty output sets refuse. Notice bytes must be nonempty UTF-8, contained regular files; exact notice bytes, paths, selected policy and artifact inventory digests bind codkitDistributionNotices:1. Changed output snapshots or notice bytes refuse, and report status follows actual problems. This receipt proves named attachment and observed bytes only; approval of notice content, provenance, source carriers and SBOM remain separate distribution requirements, never inferred legal approval.

p.DISTRIBUTION-PROVENANCE: codkitDistributionDeclaration:1 maps each delivered payload file/link to inspected source paths and an explicit license expression. Every actual payload is covered exactly once; missing, duplicate, extra or uninspected paths refuse. Only trusted composition can approve regular-file metadata exclusions after their notice/SBOM checks; declaration alone cannot hide a payload. Fresh consumer inspection must be complete and nonempty. Foreign holders and origin-registry evidence stay in third-party scope. Complete source expressions, including AND/OR/WITH, are preserved; multiple distinct expressions require their deterministic parenthesized AND combination to be explicitly approved by policy, never an inferred permission or rewritten upstream obligation. Actual source/carrier/registry bytes, authority/store/additional prohibitions, declaration and payload hashes bind codkitDistributionProvenance:1. Before/after source and artifact inspections refuse moved snapshots. The build mapping remains a declaration, not a cryptographic proof of compilation or an external legal approval.

p.DISTRIBUTION-DOCUMENTS: The deterministic version-1 NOTICE content and selected SPDX-2.3 JSON export derive from policy-checked payload provenance, not from absent minified headers. Notice includes component, selected authority, inspected sources/carriers/origin and exact trusted texts for every used standard/custom license and exception. A standard SPDX identifier alone never substitutes for its required notice text; missing or mismatched trusted text refuses. SPDX binds every declared payload path and SHA-256, explicit license conclusion, source mapping and exact extracted LicenseRef text; file-level copyright and in-file license information are not invented from source. Metadata files are excluded from document-content digests to avoid self-reference; adding finalized NOTICE/SBOM leaves expected documents unchanged while final inventory receipts still bind their bytes. SPDX creation time is an explicit whole-second UTC timestamp; namespace changes with document content. Moved authority, invalid identities/time and tampered custom text refuse. Attached documents must match expected UTF-8 bytes exactly and actual payload receipts still match. No general SPDX importer or eternal SBOM choice is promised; the strict owned export subset is versioned by external SPDX-2.3 and validated against that version.

p.ORGANIZATION-DISTRIBUTION-EVIDENCE: Consumer source scanning, actual artifact NOTICE/carrier checks and selected SBOM export must bind the selected trusted policy before package/publish enforcement is accepted. A minified artifact without required attached notice is incomplete/red even when source headers were valid. Report evidence complete/incomplete, never a legal-compatibility ruling. Mechanism fixtures are labelled examples, not real commercial approvals or external partner evidence.
